description: Why Cast AI? Cast AI is an automation platform that operates cloud-native and AI infrastructure at scale. By embedding autonomous decision-making directly into Kubernetes and cloud environments, Cast AI continuously optimizes performance, reliability, and efficiency in production. The old way doesn't work. As Kubernetes and AI environments grow, manual decisions don’t. Cast AI replaces tickets, alerts, and manual tuning with continuous automation that adapts infrastructure as conditions change. Efficiency and cost savings follow naturally from that automation. Over 2,100 companies already rely on Cast AI, including Akamai, BMW, Cisco, FICO, HuggingFace, NielsenIQ, Swisscom, and TGS. Global team, diverse perspectives We're headquartered in Miami, but our impact is international. We take a global and intentional approach to diversity. Today, Cast AI operates across 34 countries spanning Europe, North America, Latin America, and APAC, bringing a wide range of perspectives into how we build and lead. Unicorn momentum In January 2026, we achieved unicorn status with a strategic investment from Pacific Alliance Ventures, the corporate venture arm of Shinsegae Group (a $50+ billion Korean conglomerate). Our valuation now exceeds $1 billion, and we're just getting started. Join us as we build the future of autonomous infrastructure. About The Role Kimchi is building products at the frontier of how engineering organizations adopt and operate AI — across AI coding and agents, inference, model orchestration, governance, and the infrastructure that makes all of it work reliably at scale. This is a highly dynamic space. Customer expectations, technology capabilities, competitors, and even the problems worth solving are changing quickly. That means we’re looking for a Senior Product Manager who is exceptionally good at working before the problem is well defined. You won’t inherit a neat backlog of customer requirements and execute against it. You’ll be expected to explore emerging problem spaces, talk to customers, understand technology shifts, connect weak signals, form hypotheses, and decide which problems are important enough for Kimchi to solve. A large part of the job is turning ambiguity into clarity while operating in a dynamic greenfield environment. You’ll work closely with engineering, design, customers, and GTM to take promising opportunities from an initial insight through validation, 0→1 product development, adoption, and iteration. What We're Looking For Significant experience owning software products end-to-end, with the judgment and independence expected from a Senior Product Manager. Strong 0→1 experience. You have personally taken products or significant product areas from an unclear opportunity through discovery, validation, launch, and iteration. A track record of navigating ambiguity. You can give examples where neither the problem nor the solution was obvious at the beginning and explain how you created clarity. Excellent problem selection and product judgment. You don’t just solve problems well; you are deliberate about deciding which problems are worth solving in the first place. Experience working in greenfield, rapidly changing, or emerging domains where information is incomplete and plans frequently need to change. Strong customer discovery skills. You can go beyond what customers ask for and uncover the underlying problem, context, and behavior. Strong analytical thinking. You are comfortable combining qualitative evidence, product data, market signals, and technical constraints to make decisions. Strong written and verbal communication. You can simplify complex topics without oversimplifying the underlying problem. Experience working closely with highly technical engineering teams and enough technical curiosity to understand the systems you are building. A bias toward experimentation and learning rather than large upfront plans. Comfort making decisions with imperfect information and changing your mind when new evidence emerges. Hands-on use of modern AI tools in your own work. You should be actively exploring how LLMs and agents change both the products we build and the way product work itself gets done. What Would Make You Stand Out You don’t need to check every box, but we’d be especially interested if you have experience with one or more of: Developer tools or products built for software engineers AI/ML products, LLM infrastructure, AI agents, or AI-powered developer tools Infrastructure, platforms, APIs, or technically complex B2B products Products where the primary challenge was discovering product-market fit rather than optimizing an established product Early-stage startups or new product initiatives inside larger companies Enterprise products where you have had direct access to customers during discovery and product development Responsibilities Identify problems worth solving. Explore customer needs, usage data, technology shifts, competitive products, and market signals to determine where Kimchi should invest. Turn ambiguity into product direction. Take broad or poorly understood opportunities and structure them into clear problems, hypotheses, assumptions, and experiments. Lead 0→1 product development. Move from an insight or hypothesis to a real product that customers can use, learn from, and ultimately depend on. Validate before scaling. Find the fastest way to test whether a problem matters and whether our proposed solution creates meaningful value. Be equally comfortable investing further or killing an idea when the evidence says we should. Make hard prioritization decisions. There will always be more interesting opportunities than we can pursue. You’ll decide what deserves attention now, what can wait, and what we should deliberately not build. Work directly with customers. Run discovery, observe workflows, understand underlying motivations and constraints, and distinguish individual requests from broader problems. Partner deeply with engineering and design. Shape solutions collaboratively. Understand enough of the technology to explore possibilities and trade-offs with strong technical teams. Define what success means. Establish the customer and business outcomes we expect, determine how to measure them, and use evidence to guide subsequent decisions. Drive adoption, not just launches. Stay accountable after something ships. Understand whether customers are discovering it, using it repeatedly, getting value from it, and why. Communicate clearly. Write concise product narratives, one-pagers, PRDs, and decision documents that make complex problems understandable and align teams around what matters and why. We are a distributed team, so exceptional writing skills are essential for every member. Help shape Kimchi itself. This is still a rapidly evolving product and organization. You’ll influence not only individual features, but how we think about the product, our customers, and the market. What’s in it for you? Competitive salary Enjoy a flexible, remote-first global environment. Collaborate with a global team of cloud experts and innovators, passionate about pushing the boundaries of Kubernetes technology. Equity options. Get quick feedback with a fast-paced workflow. Most feature projects are completed in 1 to 4 weeks. Spend 10% of your work time on personal projects or self-improvement. Learning budget for professional and personal development - including access to international conferences and courses that elevate your skills. Annual hackathon to spark new ideas and strengthen team bonds. Team-building budget and company events to connect with your colleagues. Equipment budget to ensure you have everything you need. Extra days off to help maintain a healthy work-life balance. As part of our standard hiring process, we would like to inform you that a background check may be conducted at the final stage of recruitment through our third-party provider, Checkr. Please note that Cast AI does not provide any form of visa sponsorship/work permit.

description: Description Broadway Gaming is a dynamic and expanding online gaming company operating mainly in the UK gaming market. We offer Bingo, Casino and Slot products across multiple brands. We have office locations in Dublin, UK, Tel Aviv, Romania and India. We're looking for a commercially minded, hands-on Growth Marketing Manager to help grow and optimise our newly launched prize draw business. We're an established UKGC-regulated bingo and casino operator expanding into the prize draw market. You'll work across growth, acquisition, CRM, prizes, content and performance, with support from senior stakeholders and specialist teams across the business. At our core, we live by five key values that shape everything we do: • Customers First – We create every experience with our customers at heart. • Bring the Fun – Passion and fun fuel everything we do. • Always Evolving – We stay curious, brave, and ready to reinvent. • Better Together – Collaboration makes us stronger, smarter, unstoppable. • Do What’s Right – We act with honesty, fairness, and accountability — always. Benefits Hybrid work from home model. Competitive Salary (DOE). Discretionary Annual Performance Bonus. Company funded health insurance. Personal life insurance and Income protection. Tax Saver Scheme. Bike to Work. Company Social events, pool tournaments and much more fun. City Centre Location. This is an opportunity to help shape a new business proposition, rather than simply manage an established programme. You'll have real ownership across growth and commercial performance, with the support of experienced teams across the wider business.

description: 🏡 About Korners Korners is the company behind Kurtains, the UAE's leading made to measure curtains and blinds service, along with Floorz for flooring and MAKAN for furniture rental. We're a team of 80 people, we transform more than 1,000 homes every month, and we're growing fast. We're building the GCC's platform for custom home services. Curtains, blinds and flooring all need expert advice, precise measurement, and professional installation, yet buying them still means endless calls, changing quotes, and no idea what a fair price is. We replaced that with a simple promise: an instant online estimate, an expert visit at home, and a final price that never moves. Our model is what makes this role exciting. We win the customer, and our technology coordinates a network of the market's best suppliers to deliver. That makes growth a key engine of the company. What's next: Scale our existing categories Launch new home categories Launch new markets, starting with Saudi Arabia Our ambition: by 2030, Korners has changed how the GCC shapes its homes. Every major home category, in every major city in the region. 🎯 About the role We're looking for a Growth Manager with strong analytical thinking and sound business judgment, who uses AI to move faster, to drive growth across Korners' brands. Working closely with Youssef, our Co-CEO, you'll understand our customer funnel, identify the biggest opportunities, run experiments, and turn data into decisions that improve acquisition, conversion, and revenue. You may bring deep expertise in one growth discipline or experience across several. Whether your background is in performance marketing, CRM, SEO, or conversion optimization, what matters is your ability to diagnose problems, test ideas rigorously, and deliver measurable business results. This role gives you the opportunity to expand your scope across channels, brands, and markets. You'll combine direct execution with the coordination of internal teams, external specialists, and AI agents. This is an analytical role. You'll spend a large part of your time in data, funnels, and numbers. If you prefer creative or brand work, this isn't the right fit. 🚀 What You'll Own Growth priorities: identify the biggest opportunities across acquisition, conversion, and customer lifecycle, and focus resources where they can deliver the greatest business impact. Customer acquisition: improve performance across paid marketing, CRM, SEO, and new channels, balancing scale and acquisition costs. Full funnel conversion: work with marketing, tech, sales, and operations to improve the journey from first interaction to booking, completed visit, quotation, and purchase. CRM and lifecycle growth: develop nurturing, reactivation, referral, and cross selling initiatives across our verticals. Analytics and experimentation: strengthen measurement, diagnose performance changes, run structured tests, and translate findings into decisions that improve revenue and unit economics. AI and agents in growth: design, deploy, and improve AI agents that handle recurring growth work, Coordinate specialists: give agencies and freelancers clear objectives, challenge recommendations, and follow through on results. New growth opportunities: support launches into new categories and markets, building repeatable approaches as we scale. You'll build on your existing strengths and expand into other areas, combining direct execution with support from internal teams, external specialists, and AI. 📌 About you 3 to 7 years of relevant growth experience, ideally within a B2C business or growth agency. Proven results in at least one growth discipline. Broader experience is welcome, but expertise across every channel is not required. Strong analytical thinking: you can break down a funnel, question data quality, identify the drivers of performance, and decide what to investigate next. Customer understanding and business judgment: understand our ideal customers, their needs, and buying motivations to shape acquisition strategies and experiments. Ownership from start to finish: lead projects from identifying the problem through execution, coordinate stakeholders, and take responsibility for the outcome. Business outcomes over channel metrics: you measure success in completed sales and margin, not clicks, and you automate your own work to take on more. Comfort working directly with spreadsheets, analytics tools, and dashboards. AI fluency: you use LLMs daily in your work and have built or configured at least one AI workflow or agent that saved real time or improved results. Coding is a plus, not a requirement. Curiosity and a bias to automate are. Clear communication, structured prioritization, and consistent follow through. 🌱 Why Join Korners Shape the next stage: build the channels, partnerships, and systems that will take us to new heights See your impact firsthand: work directly with ambitious teams, with meaningful ownership and limited bureaucracy. Grow through real responsibility: broaden your commercial, analytical, and leadership skills across brands and markets. Share in the upside: competitive compensation, bonus, and stock options. 💡 How We Work Our culture combines ambition and accountability with empathy and respect. Outgrow Yourself: keep expanding your skills, judgment, and impact as the company grows. Own It End to End: manage dependencies, raise blockers early, and follow through on commitments. Structure the Chaos: bring clarity to ambiguity and use evidence to guide decisions. People, Not Machines: hold high standards while treating people with fairness and understanding. Challenge Every Limit: question the default, test new approaches, and take on unfamiliar problems. ✉️ Our Application Process Our process includes an introductory call, followed by interviews with the cofounders covering fit and a practical case study.

description: Read this part first Most of this system is built by coding agents. Delivery capacity is not our constraint — deciding what should exist is. That is the whole of this role. You will not receive requirements. You will go and find out what a trader, an operator, an economist and a financier actually do, write the definition of each of those jobs yourself, and turn it into a working prototype of the system. You will own the backlog and the sprint scope for your layer: what is ready, what enters a sprint, what ships, what gets cut. And you will say no to the business when no is the right answer, and defend it in the demo, with the people who asked for it in the room. If that reads as too much authority for one person, it is not the job you are looking for. If it reads as the first product job in years that isn't ticket administration, keep going. The product We are building the system an international oil-products trader will run its business on: the full deal lifecycle from contract to settlement. Pricing against Platts and Argus formulas. Costs accumulating across a chain of vessels, rail, trucks and storage. Invoicing, inventory, losses, claims, hedging. The purpose of the whole thing is that anyone involved in a deal can reconstruct the P&L between any two points of the chain, at any moment, on an agreed basis. Real money moves on the numbers it produces. Correctness is the product. Today that business runs on spreadsheets, email and phone calls, plus six years of an attempt that never shipped. Our backend team is well ahead — the transactional core is being built. What does not exist anywhere, in any document or any legacy screen, is the product logic: what each role sees, in what order, with what hidden from them, and what the system should already know before it asks. That is the layer you own. About The Role Four core users, each with a completely different relationship to the same deal: The trader — orchestrates and monitors, does not type. Open and closed positions, where the goods are, what was earned and lost. The operator — the coordination surface. Routes, vessels, counterparties, load and discharge, documents, the thousand small facts that make a cargo happen. The economist — deal economics, and matching every invoice line against contract terms. Target: heavy automation. The financier — cash, payments, allocation, offset, what is needed tomorrow and in which currency. Plus logistics roles, inspectors, and management who want the business explained to them rather than tabulated. The interesting constraints are real ones. Junior and head trader use the same screens with different scope. The system pre-fills what it can infer and asks only what it cannot, with reasons attached. No two deals have the same contract terms, so forms cannot be a fixed checklist. And the executive sponsor of this platform will never be a daily user, while the daily users have been asked for their input for six years and have watched nothing ship. Holding those two audiences together is not a communication tax on the job — it is a large part of the job. Day to day Interview the trading company's own people and read their documents until you can argue with them; write the role definitions yourself- Take prototypes to the business, get them signed off, and keep them signed off- Own readiness and sprint scope for your layer, in two-week sprints against an explicit Definition of Ready and Definition of Done Cut things. Explain the cut to the person who wanted it. Decide what each screen needs from the platform underneath — which data, which calculation, which service — and get engineering to commit to it - Prototype the whole system as screens, early and fast, with AI producing the first version of nearly everything What you need 5+ years in product management on complex B2B systems — trading, fintech, logistics, ERP, or anything where a wrong number costs somebody money AI as your primary way of working. This is a requirement, not a preference. Agents draft our role descriptions, specifications, screen flows, test data and analysis. Your value is direction and verification: framing the problem, structuring the context, and catching the answer that is fluent and wrong. If your use of AI is asking a chatbot to tidy your prose, you will be slower than this team runs You can absorb an unfamiliar domain at speed — pricing formulas, Incoterms, demurrage, cost accrual, netback — through interviews and documents, without losing the detail that turns out to matter Fluent Russian; English good enough to run a working session with the client's people Strongly preferred Commodity trading, CTRM/ETRM, or a middle/back-office system in a trading house Having designed screens yourself — wireframe level, not visual Experience where the sponsor of the project was not one of its users You decide with incomplete information, and you can be publicly wrong and correct it without losing the room You source information yourself. No BA upstream of you, no analyst to delegate discovery to At least one large system you personally took from nothing to daily use. Not a redesign, not a module inside someone else's roadmap, not a pilot that ended at the pilot. People whose jobs depend on it, using it every day What we offer Ownership of the product layer, end to end, with the authority that requires Direct access to founders and decision-makers on both sides; no account manager in between A serious, unsolved domain problem rather than another CRUD product Generous AI tooling budget — frontier models are a working expense, not a perk Fully remote and long-term, with regular travel to Dubai Competitive compensation, discussed individually Honestly about the pace The first production release is scheduled for February. Until then the intensity is high and the domain is unforgiving. That is the trade for the autonomy. How to apply Send your CV plus answers to all four questions. Applications without answers are not reviewed. Pick one specific job title you have built a product for. What did you decide that person should not see on their screen, and how did you hold that position when they asked for it? A senior stakeholder who is not a user signs off on your prototype, then rejects it at the demo two weeks later, in front of the team that has to build it. What do you do that week — and what do you change so it does not repeat? Show us a real piece of work you produced by directing an AI: a specification, a role description, a research synthesis. Include the brief you gave it. Then one case where the output was plausible and wrong — how you caught it, and what check you now run every time. Something you cut or refused to build under pressure. What was your argument, who was unhappy, and what actually happened.

description: For an international organisation whose work has a clear social purpose, this is an opportunity to help shape how product decisions are made across its digital platforms. You will work closely with Product, Design and Engineering to understand what users do, evaluate changes and make results useful for decision-making. The focus is on measurement, experimentation and reliable evidence , rather than building machine learning models for production. What you'll do Design A/B tests and use causal methods when controlled testing is not possible. Define success metrics and check whether they measure the outcomes that matter. Analyse adoption, retention, funnels and user behaviour across different groups. Use statistical models to understand results, test assumptions and communicate uncertainty. Set clear standards for analysis and help colleagues assess the quality of their findings. Work with engineers to improve tracking, documentation and data quality. Evaluate AI tools that support analysis, including how their answers are checked. Turn complex findings into concise recommendations for product teams and senior stakeholders. What you bring 3+ years of experience in statistical modelling or machine learning . Strong SQL skills and fluency in Python or R . Experience designing experiments and applying causal methods when randomisation is not possible. A solid understanding of regression, multilevel models and statistical uncertainty. Experience with product analytics, including funnels, cohorts, retention and adoption. A strong eye for data quality and the ability to work closely with Product, Design and Engineering. Clear communication skills, including the confidence to explain what the data cannot establish. Experience with BI tools, survey research or behavioural research methods is a plus The challenge A product change can improve one metric without improving the outcome that matters. Sometimes a controlled experiment is possible. Often, users are part of different groups or a change reaches them at different times. Your challenge is to build evidence that teams can trust and use . That means choosing the right measures, understanding the limits of the data and making the findings clear enough to guide a decision. How do you establish whether a change made a difference? Which comparisons are valid? And how do you help teams act on the results without overstating what the data proves? Package In addition to the competitive salary, the package includes an Individual Choice Budget (12%), profit sharing, a pension plan under the applicable CLA, remote work options and additional employment benefits.
